questions_and_answers.question_text: What may stand in front of bìyè with no prepositional verb?
Which two prepositional verbs may precede bìyè?
What kind of compound is bìyè, and what does this allow?
In which construction does the separation of bì and yè most often occur?
What are the three meanings of wèntí?
Write the Chinese for "He graduated from Taiwan University."
Write the Chinese for "He graduated in 1976," separating bì and yè.
Write the Chinese for "I graduated last year from the University of Texas."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ qùnián cóng Dézhōu Dàxué bìyè le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the two possible meanings of Nǐ yǒu wèntí ma?

answers.answer_text: "Do you have any questions?" or "Are you having any problems?"

5. A: Bú rènshi.                     I don't know him.
   A: Búguò tīngshuō tā yě shi       However, I have heard that he also
      Jiāzhōu Dàxué bìyède, suǒyǐ     graduated from the University of
      xiǎng qǐng ni gěi wo jièshao    California, so I wanted to ask
      jièshao.                        you to introduce me to him.

6. B: Méi wèntí. Wǒ kànkan...hǎo,    No problem. I'll take a look....
      wǒmen xiànzài dōu yǒu           Okay, we are both free now.
      gōngfu.
   B: Nǐ xiànzài néng lái ma?        Can you come now?

Note on No. 5

Shi Jiāzhōu Dàxué bìyède, "graduated from the University of California": The name of a school or a word describing the type of school may stand in front of the verb bìyè with no preceding prepositional verb, such as cóng, "from."

Nǐ érzi yǐjing dàxué/zhōngxué/    Has your son graduated from college/
xiǎoxué bìyè le ma?               high school/elementary school already?
Tā dàxué hái méi bìyè ne.        He has not graduated from college yet.
Tā shi Táiwān Dàxué bìyède.      He graduated from Taiwan University.

Bìyè may also be preceded by either zài, "at," or cóng, "from."

Nǐ shi zài něige zhōngxué        What high school did you graduate
bìyède?                          from?
Wǒ qùnián cóng Dézhōu Dàxué      I graduated last year from the
bìyè le.                         University of Texas.

Bìyè, meaning "to complete a course of study," is a compound made up of a verb plus a general object. For this reason, the object yè may be separated from the verb bì. This separation occurs most frequently in sentences containing the shi...de construction.

Tā shi yījiǔqīliùnián bìde yè.   He graduated in 1976.

Note on No. 6

The noun wèntí can mean "question," "problem," or "difficulty."

Tā wènle hǎoduō wèntí.           He asked a lot of questions.
Nà shi yíge hěn dàde wèntí.      That's a big problem.

Nǐ yǒu wèntí ma? could mean either "Do you have any questions?" or "Are you having any problems?"
